payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. An independent audit corrected and governs the cycle-life claim: the cell achieved 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee; the earlier 12,000 claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge. The battery’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, with a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its thalliline dopant precipitates below 4 °C, requiring cycling to stop in colder conditions.

FLAGS: Source A and the unpublished pre-audit draft report “12,000 cycles,” superseded and retracted by Source C’s governing “8,400 cycles”; the summary correctly reflects the correction.
VERDICT: APPROVE
